evidence.claim: The federal executive authority is exercised through the Prime Minister, who is the chief executive of the Federation, and the Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly.
evidence.title: Chapter 3: The Federal Government
evidence.publisher: pakistani.org (text of the Constitution of Pakistan)
evidence.excerpt: The federal executive authority is exercised through the Prime Minister, who is the chief executive of the Federation, and the Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct constitutional text from the governing legal framework.
evidence.period_fit: Directly applicable to 2022 office authority and parliamentary dependence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Shehbaz Sharif's formal office and confidence dependence, but not personal control of nuclear policy.
contrary_evidence: Formal chief-executive status does not prove direct operational control over nuclear forces or security institutions.

evidence.claim: The Federal Government has control and command of the Armed Forces.
evidence.title: Chapter 2: Armed Forces
evidence.publisher: pakistani.org (text of the Constitution of Pakistan)
evidence.excerpt: The Federal Government has control and command of the Armed Forces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct constitutional text on state command authority.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows the formal state command structure under Sharif's government, but not a target-period nuclear decision by Sharif personally.
contrary_evidence: This general command clause does not by itself show day-to-day nuclear command or how much practical autonomy the military retained.

evidence.claim: After India's accidental missile launch, Pakistan demanded a joint probe and raised serious concerns about security protocols and technical safeguards against accidental or unauthorized launch in a nuclearized environment.
evidence.title: Transcript of the Press Briefing by Spokesperson on Friday, 18 March, 2022
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: After India's accidental missile launch, Pakistan demanded a joint probe and raised serious concerns about security protocols and technical safeguards against accidental or unauthorized launch in a nuclearized environment.
evidence.source_locator: Q&A and response paragraphs on the missile incident
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated official transcript of the government's response in the crisis moment.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period and directly about a 2022 crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the government under Sharif, though the transcript is from the foreign ministry rather than Sharif personally.
contrary_evidence: The response was also highly accusatory, so it is mixed evidence: de-escalatory in process but escalatory in tone.

evidence.claim: India said it was reviewing procedures after accidentally firing a missile into Pakistan during routine maintenance.
evidence.title: India says reviewing procedures after missile accidentally fired into Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: India said it was reviewing procedures after accidentally firing a missile into Pakistan during routine maintenance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is a strong independent corroborator of the incident context.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period, corroborating the March 2022 crisis context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context only; the incident originated in India, not from Sharif's own action.
contrary_evidence: This does not show Sharif's conduct directly, only the external crisis he had to manage.

evidence.claim: Pakistan reportedly keeps its nuclear weapons de-mated, with a strict centralized command-and-control system in place, and maintains a unilateral moratorium on nuclear testing.
evidence.title: Pakistan's Evolving Nuclear Doctrine
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan reportedly keeps its nuclear weapons de-mated, with a strict centralized command-and-control system in place, and maintains a unilateral moratorium on nuclear testing.
evidence.source_locator: doctrine discussion on de-mated weapons, centralized command and control, and testing moratorium
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Strong secondary synthesis, but retrospective and not a 2022 primary record.
evidence.period_fit: Useful inherited-structure context for 2022, though written later.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Background only; it describes a standing doctrine and security architecture rather than a Sharif-specific 2022 decision.
contrary_evidence: This remains a long-standing doctrine summary, not evidence that Sharif improved or worsened it in 2022.
